correctness.rationale: For every eligible simplex dimension, skeleton order, and summand count, exact coordinate induction on appropriately many masses gives a fixed collection of unit-sum sparse rows whenever the support-capacity threshold is met. The first admissible consecutive mass window exists because the smallest window has total mass strictly below one. Its donor exists by strict excess of the preceding window, or the average-of-largest-entries inequality at the leading window. Exactly the intended number of entries are removed, preserving the induction length and total mass. The necessity witness takes a positive parameter smaller than the reciprocal summand count, forcing every summand to include one common vertex; the resulting strict support-capacity shortage contradicts the positive target coordinates. The standalone exact-Fraction tests checked 4410 cases but are not the proof.
